subject: Ciências
description_pt: Aplicar os conhecimentos sobre as mudanças de estado físico da água para explicar o ciclo hidrológico e analisar suas implicações na agricultura, no clima, na geração de energia elétrica, no provimento de água potável e no equilíbrio dos ecossistemas regionais (ou locais).

components.description_pt: Explicar o ciclo da água utilizando conhecimentos sobre estados físicos da água e suas mudanças
components.description_en: Explain the water cycle using knowledge of the physical states of water and their changes
components.cc_component_description: Explain the roles of evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, and surface flow in the water cycle

components.description_pt: Relacionar o ciclo da água a fenômenos como regulação climática e qualidade do ar atmosférico
components.description_en: Relate the water cycle to phenomena such as climate regulation and atmospheric air quality
components.cc_component_description: Explain how water's high heat capacity affects Earth's energy storage and climate regulation

components.description_pt: Analisar implicações do ciclo da água para agricultura, geração de energia elétrica e abastecimento de água potável
components.description_en: Analyze the implications of the water cycle for agriculture, electric power generation, and drinking water supply
components.cc_component_description: Analyze the limitations of fresh water, mineral, and biosphere resources relative to human demand

components.description_pt: Conectar perturbações no ciclo da água a impactos em ecossistemas regionais ou locais
components.description_en: Connect disruptions in the water cycle to impacts on regional or local ecosystems
components.cc_component_description: Explain how ecosystems change over time due to natural variation or external disruptions

cc_matches.description: Water continually cycles among land, ocean, and atmosphere via transpiration, evaporation, condensation and crystallization, and precipitation, as well as downhill flows on land.

Humans depend on Earth’s land, ocean, atmosphere, and biosphere for many different resources. Minerals, fresh water, and biosphere resources are limited, and many are not renewable or replaceable over human lifetimes. These resources are distributed unevenly around the planet as a result of past geologic processes.
Ecosystems are dynamic in nature; their characteristics can vary over time. Disruptions to any physical or biological component of an ecosystem can lead to shifts in all its populations.

The abundance of liquid water on Earth’s surface and its unique combination of physical and chemical properties are central to the planet’s dynamics. These properties include water’s exceptional capacity to absorb, store, and release large amounts of energy, transmit sunlight, expand upon freezing, dissolve and transport materials, and lower the viscosities and melting points of rocks.
